newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House Commerce panel announces restructuring.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House Commerce panel announces restructuring.

text.p: U.S. House Commerce Committee Chairman Rep. Thomas Bliley, R-Va., announced the creation of two new subpanels - the subcommittee on finance and hazardous materials and the subcommittee on telecommunications, trade, and consumer protection.
The panels will be chaired by Rep. Mike Oxley, R-Ohio, and Rep. Billy Tauzin, R-La., respectively.

They represent a restructuring of two subcommittees - the commerce, trade and hazardous materials subpanel, which was chaired by Oxley, and the telecommunications and finance subcommittee, which was chaired by Rep. Jack Fields, R-Texas. Fields did not run for relection.

"This is a win-win situation for everyone," Tauzin said in a press statement. "Clearly this realignment will facilitate our efforts to move important reform legislation forward during the 105th Congress."
Oxley's new finance and hazardous materials subpanel will have jurisdiction over five broad topics.

They are securities and finance; solid waste, hazardous waste and toxic substances, including Superfund and the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act; noise pollution control; insurance (except health insurance); and regulation of travel, tourism and time.

Oxley said Superfund reform will be a "priority" for his panel. "On securites, I'll be working with Chairman Arthur Levitt at the SEC toward making the American Capital markets the best in the world," Oxley said.
Tauzin's new telecommunications, trade and consumer protection subpanel also will oversee five areas.

They are interstate and foreign telecommunications; interstate and foreign commerce; regulation of commercial practices (the Federal Trade Commission); consumer protection in general, consumer product safey, and product liability; and motor vehicle safety.

The other House Commerce subpanels will have unchanged chairmen and jurisdictions, Bliley said. Rep. Joe Barton, R-Texaas, will continue to chair the oversight and investigation subpanel, Bliley said.
Rep. Dan Schaefer, R-Colo., returns as chairman of the energy and power panel. And Rep. Michael Bilirakis, R-Fl., will again chair the health and environment subcommittee, Bliley said.
